intended_object: The ℝ-algebra isomorphism ℝ[X]/(p) ≅ ℂ for an irreducible real quadratic p, given by evaluating polynomial classes at a chosen complex root z of p (so X ↦ z). This is from the docstring and the module doc, which cites Vakil, Exercise 3.2.B.
explanation:
The definition chains two equivalences. The first is the library's general `adjoinRootEquivOfRoot`, an equivalence AdjoinRoot p ≃ QuadraticAlgebra R (-1) 0 over any field. It is built from `AdjoinRoot.liftAlgHom` sending the root to the given element, and is bijective because both sides have dimension 2. The second is `realComplexEquiv : QuadraticAlgebra ℝ (-1) 0 ≃ ℂ`. The root z is carried across `realComplexEquiv.symm`, and the companion lemmas show that the composite sends `AdjoinRoot.root p` to z and `mk g` to g(z). So the result is exactly the evaluation isomorphism ℝ[X]/(p) ≅ ℂ, X ↦ z.

The hypotheses are right. Since p is irreducible, it is nonzero and (p) is maximal. Since its degree is 2, the quotient is 2-dimensional, so the injective map into ℂ is bijective. Nothing in the definition forces z to be one root rather than the other (the docstring says so on purpose), and nothing is wrong in degenerate cases.

On generality: Mathlib has a general way to build such equivalences from power bases (`AdjoinRoot.equiv'`, which needs a `PowerBasis` of the target), and the library itself has a field-general version (`adjoinRootEquivOfRoot`). This definition is the specific ℝ/ℂ instance that the Vakil exercise asks for. Its target is the specific algebra ℂ, so it is a specific object, not a general notion written out in an unnecessarily narrow setting. Since the general step is already factored out separately, the definition is faithful.
